Needs either a substrate worktree grant or an approved publish of the engine's adapters package. A sixth live setback producer (bastrop-per-parcel-setback.ts:75) has no test locking in its numeric output.
P-167: re-run scripts/surface-probe.mjs --rows P-167 now that engine-api has redeployed since the original close, to see if the PDF leg is measurable; if not, name the specific blocker.

P-158: factory-parcel-building-footprint-reconcile was not run this wave (feeds a different, cell-level read path than this row's own predicate); it also still has no staging target, a gap named in the phase-2 close and never fixed.

P-152: item 2 (panel dollar rails + owner gated in the BFF) remains deliberately deferred -- a real, non-trivial entitlement-gate change the lane judged unsafe to ship unreviewed in one pass. Item 5's engine-side entitlement gate is still absent (smartsite-mcp has no entitlement check at all; the engine never reads accessTier to gate anything).

Two lessons for the fleet, worth carrying into future large-data-job rows: (1) a DISTINCT ON or pagination key must match a table's actual primary key exactly or silent data loss is possible with no visible error; (2) verify a large job's query plan with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before trusting it to finish inside any configured timeout -- a missing composite index cost this wave most of a day.

Process note: this wave's async single-shot lane model meant CP1/CP2 design review happened after the fact (adversarial review of the final report) rather than mid-task for most rows; several lanes disclosed this gap themselves rather than pretending a live checkpoint had occurred. Worth a standing decision on whether this program's lane model should build in an actual mid-task pause point, or formally accept post-hoc adversarial review as this program's real checkpoint mechanism.
